the dihadron FF's from the NJL-Jet model are evolved from their model scale to a scale typical of experimental measurements and that the evolution has a significant impact on the shapes of dihadron fragmentation function.

The dihadron fragmentation function for $u\to\pi^+\pi^- $ is significantly affected by evolution from the model scale $\Lambda_{\text{QCD}}^2$ to a typical experimental energy scale of $4\text{GeV}^ 2$.
the evolution of the dihadrons is significant for the doubly favored process and the $K^+K^−$ process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of dihadrons in $e^+ e^-$ annihilation, where the fragmentation of a quark or an antiquark produces a pair of hadrons.
the study of dihadron fragmentation function in the framework of the NJL-jetty model.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dihadron fragmentation function calculations from the NJL-Jet model are now available in a form suitable for experimental comparison.
the evolution of dihadron fragmentation function is a very complicated process and that the results of this evolution can only be used to make predictions for the fragmentation of light quarks.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the evolution of dihadron fragmentation function is a very important aspect of the study of dihadron production in $e^+ e^-$ annihilation.
the dihadron production is a good observable to study the fragmentation functions in the NJL-jetty model.
the NJL-jett model provides a very good framework for studying dihadron fragmentation in the light quark sector, and that the QCD evolution effects can be studied in detail.
The main takeaway from our work is that

evolution from the NJL model scale to an experimental scale of $2 \mathrm{GeV}$ or larger has little effect on the shapes of dihadron fragmentation function distributions, while the normalization is reduced by a factor of $\sim 2$.
the dihadron FFs evolve in such a way that they are more similar to one another, as compared to the fragmentation functions at the model scale.
the dihadron FFs from the NJL-Jet model can be used in phenomenological analyses of hadronic final states in $e^+ e^-$ collisions, such as the ones performed by the BaBar collaboration.
